## TL;DR

The live file-watcher path could parse review reports as ordinary tasks because it checked only a filename extension under the work directory. I made task eligibility a shared core rule: a path must be a configured task file, must not live in either report directory, and its frontmatter must explicitly contain `id`. Both startup index builders and live updates now apply that rule. The live path removes any stale mapping when a formerly indexed path no longer qualifies. Doctor’s task-file walk also omits report storage. The regression test uses a non-default `repoos/work` directory and verifies a report write emits no task event, a real task still indexes, stale in-memory data is removed, and a full rebuild drops a stale report entry.

## Work and rationale

I started from the task’s reported split behavior: startup indexing already guarded against reports and frontmatter without an ID, while the long-running watcher had its own permissive `isTaskFile` check and parsed every matching file. The appropriate fix was at the indexing boundary, so review report storage and the review/report writers remain untouched. This keeps report files available to their existing consumers while preventing them from entering the task identity space, which is what protects Delete and Archive actions from being offered for those paths.

I added `isIndexableTaskFile` in the core task module. It combines three conditions using the repository’s configured root, work directory, and task extensions: the absolute path resolves to an eligible repository-relative task path, the first directory below `workDir` is not `reports` or legacy `engineering-reports`, and the parsed frontmatter contains the `id` key. The path helper also excludes these report namespaces, which keeps other task-path consumers from treating a report as a task file. Both `buildIndex` and `buildIndexDetailedAsync` use the shared full predicate before parsing a task. Their directory walk continues to prune the two report roots early as an optimization, while the shared predicate remains the source of truth for file eligibility.

`LiveIndex` applies the same shared predicate to file contents before calling `parseTask`. Its initial watcher-scope check intentionally remains broad enough to notice Markdown changes below `workDir`, including report paths: if an older in-memory index contains a report path, an update to a report without `id` must remove that stale mapping. The existing delete handling emits a deletion only when there really was a mapped task. A new report has no mapping and therefore produces no event. A full refresh builds replacement maps from the filtered startup index, dropping stale report entries in one rebuild event.

Doctor has a separate recursive task-file walk used by layout and frontmatter diagnostics. I updated that walk to skip directories named `reports` and `engineering-reports`, so stored review and engineering output does not affect task counts or task-file diagnostics.

The regression coverage extends the existing skipped-indexer tests. It configures `workDir` as `repoos/work`, creates a report with `task: "0006"` but no `id`, and creates an ordinary task with an explicit id. It verifies the report produces no live task and no event, while the task is present. To model the legacy state that cannot be created through the corrected live path, the test seeds the LiveIndex’s old id/path maps with a stale `review-1` entry; applying the report change evicts it, and rebuilding continues to omit it. This directly covers both the live cleanup and reload recovery behavior.

## Approaches tried

I first looked for an existing helper to extend. `isTaskFilePath` already represented work-directory and extension scope, but it did not reject report directories or inspect frontmatter. I considered reusing that function alone, but that could only solve path classification; the missing-id rule would still be duplicated in each indexer and absent from live updates. I therefore retained it as a path-level helper and added the shared `isIndexableTaskFile` predicate for complete eligibility, with all three indexing paths using the latter.

I also verified why the stale-entry regression could not be expressed by first adding an id-bearing report using the corrected `applyFileChange`: the desired behavior rejects it immediately. Instead, the test models the old in-memory cache state directly, then exercises both the live path’s cleanup and a rebuild. That test setup corresponds to the production upgrade case without reopening an invalid insertion route.

The initial focused test attempt contained that incorrect assumption and failed because the report was already rejected. I corrected the setup and reran the focused test successfully through the repository gate. No report writer, report path format, or task action semantics were changed.

## Challenges and blockers

The first required scoped check failed its formatter step on `doctor.ts` and `live-index.ts`; I ran the repository formatter and restarted the check. The next local run reached the full scoped suite but several unrelated integration tests timed out under load. Following `docs/debugging-check-failures.md`, I reran the affected suites together and then reran the preview E2E alone. The debugger and host-pressure suites passed together; the preview E2E passed alone. The suite failures therefore did not reproduce in isolation.

A subsequent required check successfully validated the complete changed-path suite on RepoOS’s remote runner: all selected test files passed, including the report-index regression and the three previously failing suites. The remote rendered contrast and UI smoke checks passed, then the local guards also passed. There are no outstanding implementation blockers. The check run’s remote transfer and complete suite took several minutes, but RepoOS completed it successfully.

## Key learnings

RepoOS has two distinct indexing lifecycles: startup builders establish the authoritative index, and `LiveIndex` incrementally tracks filesystem writes. A safeguard in only one lifecycle can appear correct on a fresh start while allowing the running server to drift. Shared eligibility logic should therefore sit near task parsing and be called by both.

Report paths are bookkeeping even when their extension matches task documents. Directory exclusion prevents the startup walk from doing unnecessary work, while an identity check protects all candidate files from being turned into tasks. The live watcher needs a slightly broader observation boundary than the index predicate so it can remove stale cache entries when a path changes category.

Finally, event behavior is part of the bug contract. Rejecting a newly written report must be silent because no task was created; removing a stale cached entry may use normal deletion behavior because clients need to forget a task that the live process previously exposed. The regression checks both states and confirms a valid task remains unaffected.
